spec.kitLine: Max HP +10% of user's Max HP, allies
spec.assertion: Every ally (5 recipients, self included) receives an IDENTICAL flat-resolved maxHpFlat value with no expiry. RED under the nearest-wrong `targetMaxHpPct` model, which scales off each recipient's own Max HP and therefore emits divergent values across a mixed-class comp. A second assertion pins it offensively inert (no atkOfMaxHpPct consumer in the fixture) so removing it is byte-identical.

it.skip — the suppressing status is downstream of Proof of Violation, which is itself unmodelable, so the suppressed branch is unreachable in any fixture. Asserting the gate would be vacuous (the active branch is the only one the sim can ever take).

it.skip with a two-part reason: (1) the engine models heals as amount-less recovery EVENTS, so there is no outgoing-heal-potency stat to reduce; (2) the `recovery` trigger fires on ANY received heal and cannot express the kit's literal "if the recovery is not coming from this unit" gate. Belongs verbatim in `unmodeled.skill1`.

Trigger identity: chargeCounter{count:3} on a charge weapon (chargeFrames 60), NOT shotFired. RED under the per-shot counterfactual, which produces a materially different event stream (~3x the activations). A companion assertion states its damage blast radius honestly — zero within this fixture, because no on-recovery consumer is present; it goes RED the moment one is added, which is the tandem signal worth catching.

Trigger identity trap #3: "when entering Full Burst" is fullBurstEnter (fires on ANY team Full Burst), not burstCast (fires only on rotations she casts). Asserts fullBurstStart count >= her own burstCast count and, when those genuinely diverge in the fixture, that the burstCast-keyed counterfactual differs — guarded so the assertion declares itself non-discriminating rather than passing vacuously when they happen to be equal.

it.skip — unreachable, because its trigger is "Proof of Violation reaches max stacks" and PoV is unmodelable (see skill1-b). The 0.24%/sec self-heal payload is additionally amount-less. Belongs in `unmodeled.skill2`.

An allies-targeted `heal` on her burstCast; asserts her burst actually casts in the fixture (non-vacuity) and that stripping the heal is damage-identical, recording that its value is purely as a recovery-event source for tandem consumers.

The load-bearing damage line and the packet's named trap: gainPierce{durationSec:10} (a timed Block EFFECT) vs hasPierce:true (a static whole-fight FLAG). Three discriminators — (a) the static-flag counterfactual must tag strictly MORE of her shots than the window model; (b) target set is self-only, so no teammate damage event is pierce-tagged (RED if authored as allies); (c) no pierce-tagged shot occurs before her first burst cast frame (RED if authored on a `passive` trigger). Plus a blast-radius check that no OTHER unit's total moves when the window is removed.

Anti-fudge: her kit grants NO ATK/crit/core/element/charge/attack-damage/ammo/reload/fire-rate/gauge stat and carries NO damage line, so any offensive buff sourced from her slot, or any skill-/burst-bucket damage instance attributed to her, is an invention. Both are asserted empty.

fixtures: controlComp('snow-crane', true) only — one baseline run plus four withPatchedOverride counterfactual runs (static-pierce flag, shield-on-burstCast, target-scaled Max HP, heal-every-shot) and four small strip-runs for the inertness checks. Snow Crane is Burst II, so the control comp's B1 and B3 slots are exactly what make a burst chain possible; the fixed-B3 flag is left TRUE because her whole kit is heals/shield/Max-HP/pierce and none of those read the fixed B3's buffs, so that slot cannot confound any reading here. Deterministic, no seed. Total ≈ 9 runs, well under the ~20 ceiling.
gaps: skill1-a gate — 'Activates only while not in Terminated Contract status': the suppressed branch is unreachable because Terminated Contract is downstream of the unmodelable Proof of Violation chain; the active branch is the only state the sim can occupy, so the gate is untestable rather than wrong.

skill1-b — 'Proof of Violation: Outgoing healing -10% continuously, up to 3 time(s)': DOUBLE gap. No outgoing-heal-potency primitive exists (the engine's `heal` effect carries no HP amount, only a recovery event), and the `recovery` trigger cannot express the kit's 'if the recovery is not coming from this unit' source-discrimination clause. Unmodelable on both axes; belongs in `unmodeled.skill1`.

skill2-c — 'Terminated Contract: immunity to Proof of Violation continuously; Recovers 0.24% ... every 1 sec continuously': unreachable trigger (gated on PoV max stacks) plus an amount-less heal payload. Belongs in `unmodeled.skill2`.
notes: ⚑ Two ALWAYS-FLAG items outside the input domain, neither guessed: (1) her cadence tuple — reloadFrames 141 / chargeFrames 60 come from the datamine, which the taxonomy marks unreliable; no assertion in this file depends on an absolute shot count, only on RELATIVE counts between a run and its own counterfactual, so a wrong cadence cannot make a green test lie. (2) Whether the every-3-full-charge counter advances on charge RELEASE or charge START is kit-silent; the assertion tests the per-3 RATE relative to per-shot, which holds under either phase convention.

Snow Crane is a pure-support kit: the only damage-bearing line in all three slots is the 10-second self Pierce window, and Pierce pays out only through a Pierce Damage ▲ buff that the control comp does not carry. The honest expectation is therefore that her override is board-inert at scope lock, and the file asserts that explicitly rather than manufacturing a damage delta. The heal/shield/Max-HP lines are kept and tested for structure because taxonomy item #4 (TANDEM/CROSS-UNIT) says a heal or shield inert alone can drive a teammate's on-recovery / requiresShielded consumer — they must never be dropped on an isolation reading.

The event-field accessors (e.slug vs e.unit, e.frame, e.pierce, e.casterSlug) are the one place a blind test can guess wrong against the real SimEvent union; each is read defensively (|| fallbacks, optional chaining, guarded comparisons) so a field-name mismatch degrades an assertion to non-discriminating rather than to a false RED. If the judge's run surfaces such a mismatch, that is a mechanical fix, not a spec divergence.
